Consult Summary:
- Acute left-sided throbbing headache with visual aura, photophobia, and nausea/vomiting; clinician impression of migraine-type headache; safety-netting and symptomatic treatment advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Left-sided throbbing headache starting at mid-day today; worse with movement/leaning forward or moving head/neck.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea with two episodes of vomiting; photophobia (wearing sunglasses); blurred vision with zig-zag lines minutes before headache onset.
- Pertinent negatives: No fever, no rash, no speech difficulties, no limb numbness/weakness, no balance/coordination problems, no recent head injury.
- Prior episodes: Similar headache a few weeks ago, lasted a couple of days, improved with painkillers and rest; not usually prone to headaches.
- Past medical history: None reported.
- Family history: Mother with migraines and underactive thyroid. No known family history of brain cancer reported.
- Medications: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) for contraception, started 3 months ago (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social history: Works in fashion; reports high job stress. Lives alone. Nonsmoker. No alcohol use. No regular exercise.
- Patient concerns: Worried about brain cancer due to headache worsening with movement; reassured during visit.

Examination:

Impression:
- Migraine-type headache with features suggestive of aura (unilateral throbbing pain, visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting). Second episode within ~1 month. Clinician reassured against meningitis or brain tumor based on history.

Plan:
- Symptomatic treatment: 
  - Paracetamol (acetaminophen) or co-codamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - NSAIDs: ibuprofen or naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Headache diary to identify potential triggers.
- Consider migraine prophylactic medication if headaches become persistent; to discuss at follow-up (proposed next week).
- Safety-net advice: Seek review urgently if not improving within 2–3 days or worsening; if headache not responding to medication; if neck pain worsens; or if new focal neurological symptoms (e.g., limb weakness) or vision changes occur.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergy status; vitals; focused neurological and fundoscopic examinations; detailed medication dosing and contraindication screening; pregnancy status; full medication reconciliation; counseling regarding combined OCP use in the context of migraine with aura not documented.
● Internal conflicts: Onset character (sudden vs gradual) unclear—patient unsure. Visual symptoms noted before headache; later stated to affect both eyes—specific laterality not firmly established. Brief transcript confusion where clinician mentions “Lyme’s” without context.
● Transcript quality: Generally clear but with minor interruptions/inaudible segments; examination details not recorded.
